The bank assesses only source-supported outcomes: a firm with market power can use price discrimination to increase profit or capture additional consumer surplus under certain conditions; with perfect price discrimination, output reaches P=MC, the firm extracts all economic surplus associated with its product, and all deadweight loss is eliminated. Graphs are embedded throughout: single-price monopoly versus perfect-price-discrimination output, D/MB and MC at the efficient quantity, surplus capture, single-price monopoly deadweight loss, and different prices across buyers. No detailed memorized checklist of additional conditions for price discrimination is imposed because the CED says only “under certain conditions” without enumerating them.
